roles.comp_local: $100,000 - $200,000 USD (range stated on the multi-location req; almost certainly the US-band disclosure, not a London figure)
roles.notes: One req is posted simultaneously for Dubai, Greenwich CT, Hong Kong, London, New York, Norwalk CT and Singapore - the same gh_jid covers all, so the London seat is not separately confirmed as a headcount. Despite the 'Quantitative Developer' title this is a Python-first role supporting traders/researchers; C++ is listed only as a 'plus'. It is closer to quant-dev tooling than to low-latency C++ systems work - a weaker fit than the track label suggests. UK: candidate's HPI visa is self-sponsored; the application form asks for sponsorship status.

existing_rows_audit.detail: London office confirmed on Verition's own contact page (3rd Floor, Lucent, 1 Sherwood St., London W1F 7BL) and a live 'Quantitative Developer' req lists London among its locations: https://www.verition.com/open-positions?gh_jid=4011276007 . However the row's 'Stated Requirements' column is wrong: it describes a modern-C++/Linux-internals/low-latency profile, whereas the actual posting asks for 1-3 years of Python with data-analysis and ML libraries and lists C++ only as a 'plus'. The row's £95-145k comp figure is also unsourced - the only figure Verition states is a $100,000-$200,000 USD band on the shared multi-location req, which reads as the US pay-transparency disclosure rather than a London number. Recommend rewriting the requirements and clearing or re-sourcing the comp cell.

notes: Verition's own contact page enumerates exactly 9 offices: Greenwich CT, Norwalk CT, New York, Chicago, Miami, London, Dubai, Hong Kong and Singapore. Of these only London, Hong Kong and Singapore are in scope. There is no Tokyo, Shanghai or continental-EU office - any row placing Verition in an EU city or Tokyo is wrong. Hiring runs on Greenhouse under the board token 'veritiongroupllc'; https://www.verition.com/open-positions renders that board via an embed. Note that job-boards.greenhouse.io/veritiongroupllc/jobs/<id> 302-redirects back to verition.com, and verition.com/open-positions is JS-only so it returns no listings to a plain fetch - the readable primary source is the Greenhouse embed, https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/embed/job_board?for=veritiongroupllc and https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/embed/job_app?for=veritiongroupllc&token=<id> . All 31 live reqs were enumerated from that board on 2026-08-04. Coverage caveat: Verition's two quant reqs (Quantitative Developer, Quantitative Research Analyst) are each a single evergreen posting spanning seven cities, so it is not possible to tell from the board whether London, Hong Kong or Singapore currently has actual headcount behind it - treat city-level availability as unconfirmed and worth asking a recruiter. Excluded as out of scope: 'Treasury Engineer' (London, https://www.verition.com/open-positions?gh_jid=5124210007) is a real live London engineering req but asks for 3+ yrs of Python/Java building margin, financing and post-trade processing systems with AWS and SQL - no C++ and no low-latency content, so it does not fit the C++ track. Also excluded: London Global Payroll Associate, Human Resources Analyst and Collateral Management Analyst (non-technical); Hong Kong Operations Associate - FX Operations and Trade Operations Associate - Middle Office (operations). Verition has no ML Performance, GPU, HPC or kernel-engineering roles open anywhere - the firm's entire Technology function on the board is platform/end-user support and treasury systems, all US-based apart from the London Treasury Engineer, so the candidate's GPU-kernel and ML-infrastructure strengths have no direct target here. No compensation figure other than the $100k-$200k USD band was found on any primary source; nothing was taken from aggregators.
